svg.title: IGMP snooping is four mechanisms, not one checkbox: table, querier, mrouter port and per-port limits
svg.desc: Four panels. The snooping table records group and port and is built from snooped reports; without it the switch floods. The querier sends periodic general queries so entries stay alive; without it entries age out and video breaks every few minutes, the most common access-layer multicast fault on a pure Layer 2 VLAN with no router. The mrouter port tells the switch where the real multicast router is, either static, learned from PIM hellos, or from IGMP queries; miss it and traffic dies at the uplink. Per-port limits and fast-leave decide what happens when a host leaves: fast-leave removes the port on the leave without a last-member query, and a group limit per port stops one host from joining thousands of groups. A bottom band states the baseline that must be applied to every access VLAN.
svg.text: Four mechanisms, four different failure symptoms
"Snooping is enabled" is not a baseline. Each of the four fails in its own recognisable way.
1. THE SNOOPING TABLE
Group plus port plus VLAN
Built by reading IGMP reports in flight. No table
entry, no filtering: the group is flooded.
show ip igmp snooping groups
Fails as: whole-VLAN flooding, uplinks saturated,
wireless clients starved of airtime.
2. THE QUERIER
Sends the periodic general query
Entries are refreshed by queries. With no router in
the VLAN there is no querier, so entries age out.
ip igmp snooping querier <SVI address>
Fails as: works, freezes for a few seconds every few
minutes, recovers on its own. The classic ticket.
3. THE MROUTER PORT
Where the real multicast router lives
Learned three ways: static configuration, PIM
hello snooping, or the source of IGMP queries.
ip igmp snooping mrouter interface Gi0/1
Fails as: one host joins, the switch filters, and
nothing arrives because the uplink was pruned too.
4. FAST-LEAVE AND PER-PORT LIMITS
What happens when a host leaves
Without fast-leave the switch queries the segment
before pruning, so a zap waits for the query cycle.
A per-port group limit stops one host from joining
thousands of groups and filling the table alone.
ip igmp snooping limit groups 50
Fails as: slow channel change, or a table exhausted
THE BASELINE, PER ACCESS VLAN
snooping on + querier with the SVI address + mrouter method named + fast-leave where hosts zap + a group limit per port + a querier timer that matches the router's
Six values. A template that sets five of them is not a template, it is a future incident with a name.
Apply it in the provisioning system, not by hand: hand-applied baselines drift within two quarters.
